blog_post.body:
## What does instant coffee label mean for an Indian kitchen?

When you pick up a jar of instant coffee in your kitchen, what do you actually look at first? Most of us glance at the brand name and bypass the fine print on the back. Yet that small ingredient list tells the true story of what is in your morning cup. For instance, if you prefer an everyday blend that keeps things balanced, Ultra Blend brings 70 percent coffee and 30 percent chicory, giving you a smooth, familiar taste at about five rupees a cup with the 100g jar priced at 309 rupees. On the other hand, if you want pure coffee with zero chicory, options like Bold at 369 rupees for 100g offer agglomerated pure coffee with a strong, honest kick. Taking just five seconds to check those proportions helps you understand your brew better, letting you choose exactly what suits your palate without any hidden surprises.
